normalized.governing_thought: Keep East in 2027 and optimize it (Option K: saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M one-time), and run a capped cross-dock test.
executive_summary: Closing East does not pay once routing and handling are counted

The CFO's $1.3M is East's gross fixed cost. Serving 200k Eastern orders from Central adds $1.0M of transport (200k × $5) and $0.2M of damage: a net $0.10M a year, zero at 2028 volume, before the $0.75M exit fee
The cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today: $3 extra per order ($0.60M) outweighs the $0.45M fixed-cost reduction
Optimized retention (K) is the cheapest design in the base case: $8.44M in 2027, $0.20–0.45M a year below either closure
Closure also breaks, or cannot yet prove, the board's binding constraints

Close to Central: 90.3% network two-day rate vs the 92% contract; Central at 100% of capacity in 2027 and 108% in 2028; the $1.1M retrofit it needs is unbudgeted and would take one-time spend to $1.85M vs $0.9M authorized
Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, but from a 6-week, non-holiday pilot with no all-ZIP definition and no promotion guarantee
Retain and optimize: 95.1% network rate, Central at 47% in 2028, $0.15M one-time
Optimize now, test the cross-dock, and decide the 2029 lease at a Q3 2028 gate
Approve Option K and a capped cross-dock test (≤$0.25M) through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, measured on all ZIP codes
Waiting avoids the $0.75M early-exit fee and settles whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited; that point swings the cross-dock's cost by $0.85M a year
Drop close-to-Central: its $5-per-order penalty makes it no cheaper than today at 2028 volume, even if Central were expanded

slides.title: We tested four network designs and a deferral path against the board's four tests plus reversibility, using all-in cost and the contracted all-ZIP service KPI

claims.claim: Options evaluated: SQ status quo, K retain and optimize, C close East serve from Central, X close East use a cross-dock, D defer (middle path)
evidence: K: Saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M upfront (facility audit)
C: End the East lease in 2027 ($0.75M) and ship all 200k Eastern orders from Central at $13 each
X: two-year deal with a third-party Eastern cross-dock: $11 per order plus a $0.85M annual minimum

claims.claim: Five tests: Economics, Service, Capacity, Funding and lease, Risk
evidence: Service: At least 92% of all orders delivered within two days, network-wide, on all ZIP codes
Capacity: Central at or below its 360k certified practical capacity in 2027 and under 2028 growth (+10% East, +6% Central)
Funding: No more than $0.9M of one-time change cost in 2027; East early exit $0.75M; West lease fixed to 2030
Risk: rebuilding East-type capacity takes nine months

claims.claim: Burden of proof: closing East is hard to reverse and must pass all five tests on today's evidence. Where the evidence is incomplete, we treat it as a risk, not a pass.

slides.title: Our working hypothesis, the CEO's 'keep East open in 2027', held up under testing, but it needed three refinements

claims.claim: a Closing saves little once all costs are counted: HOLDS
evidence: Close to Central nets $0.10M a year (vs $1.3M claimed) and $0 at 2028 volume; the cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today

claims.claim: b Closing puts the 92% SLA at risk: PARTLY
evidence: Close to Central: 90.3% (fail). Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, from non-peak pilot data

claims.claim: c Central cannot absorb Eastern demand: PARTLY
evidence: True for close to Central: 108% of capacity in 2028. Not relevant to the cross-dock

claims.claim: d Keeping East fits the lease and budget: HOLDS
evidence: Lease runs to 2029 with no fee; K needs $0.15M of the $0.9M authorized

claims.claim: e Keeping East is the cheapest way to meet the SLA: HOLDS
evidence: even unoptimized, East ($8.74M) beats the only SLA-compliant closure option ($8.89M). K is cheaper still at $8.44M

claims.claim: Refined answer: Retain and optimize, not just retain; capacity only rules out close-to-Central; keep East through 2029, not permanently
evidence: Option K beats the status quo by $0.30M a year at low risk
The cross-dock fails on cost ($0.45M a year above K in the base case) and on unproven peak service
Test the cross-dock now and decide at a Q3 2028 gate

slides.title: Five claims in the board pre-read overstate the case for one side or the other and should not anchor the decision

claims.claim: “Closing East saves $1.3M a year” (CFO slide) counts East's fixed cost only
evidence: $0.10M a year before the $0.75M exit fee (–$0.65M in 2027); $0 at 2028 volume

claims.claim: Cost per shipment (CFO dashboard) is a transport KPI only
evidence: Use all-in cost: $8.44–8.89M a year by option

claims.claim: “East delivers 98% in two days” (Finance report) excludes rural deliveries
evidence: 96% all-ZIP

claims.claim: “East causes 8 pts higher renewal” (Marketing) is correlation only
evidence: Not usable as causal evidence; retention response to service is unknown

claims.claim: “Close in June 2027 and absorb at Central with today's staffing” (Cost consultant) puts Central at full load
evidence: 100% of capacity in 2027; 108% in 2028

claims.claim: These corrections cut both ways. The decision rests on the corrected figures.

evidence: Fixed cost removed: East site $1.30M a year
Transport: 200k orders × ($13 − $8) = $1.00M a year
Damage: +$0.20M a year
Break-even volume: $1.10M ÷ $5 = 220k Eastern orders, exactly the 2028 forecast
Chart values: 1.3; 1; 0.2; 0.1; 0.1 (extra orders 2028, 20k × $5); 0 (net 2028)

evidence: $0.75M exit fee: 7.5-year payback at $0.10M a year
Carrier surcharge needed to lift Eastern service above 84% (not priced)
$1.1M Central retrofit needed once 2028 growth arrives

claims.claim: Compared with Option K, close-to-Central is $0.20M a year more expensive even before these items

A lower-growth case does not rescue closure

Retaining East (96%) has 7.7 pts of headroom

claims.claim: The 84% can be lifted only with a carrier surcharge that the $13 rate does not include
We ignore Finance's 98% and the online dashboard measure. Neither is the contract KPI.

6 wks pilot length, no holiday weeks

evidence: Pilot as reported: 93.0% East, 93.9% network, +4.7 pts

normalized.recommendation: Retain and optimize East through its 2029 lease end, and use 2027–28 to test the cross-dock alternative before the lease decision. alternatives_considered.treatment: Reference case; fails economics: $0.30M a year dearer than K; passes other tests.
Passes all five tests; cheapest at $8.44M (2027); approve now ($0.15M one-time).

alternatives_considered.option: C Close East, serve from Central
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected/dropped, not deferred: net $0.10M a year vs SQ, +$0.20M vs K, 90.3% SLA fail, Central 100%/108% capacity, $1.1M retrofit unbudgeted; loses to K at any volume above 160k.

alternatives_considered.option: X Close East, use a cross-dock

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All figures are in US$, at 2027 volumes unless stated; synthetic case data

Assumes Central (94%) and West (95%) keep their current two-day rates; generous to C
The basis of the 84% (modeled) and the 93% (pilot) is not stated; the 2-pt rural gap is illustrative only
Lower-growth case (East +5%, Central +3%) is illustrative; the pack does not size it
Assumes rates and fixed costs do not change with volume
Damage under C held at $0.20M in 2028 (not scaled)
East site capacity is not stated in the pack; 220k is assumed to fit
K's $0.30M saving is an audit estimate and may not materialize
Shift renegotiation could hurt East service
Growth may fall short (marketplace promotion not contracted) or beat forecast
Customer retention response to service is unknown; Marketing's 8-pt claim is confounded
Cross-dock peak performance, damage rate and contract terms are unknown

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came in as plain text, so there were no images to read. Chart values were taken from the [Chart] series in the extraction. Some charts include helper series ('base', 'cap') that look like layout aids, and I left them out as evidence. The text for slide 9 starts with a callout pasted into the title field; I used the slide's headline sentence as the title. Slide 10's title field holds a callout ('6% of annual Eastern volume tested 12,000 orders vs 200k a year'); I used the headline sentence there too. Slide 2 states a 'Governing thought' of several sentences; governing_thought holds its first sentence, and slide 2's claims hold the rest.
